### Changed - Clicking "Empty Trash" now starts cleanup and closes the reminder immediately. The extra scan, separate confirmation, button delay and wait for a result are removed. Cleanup continues in the background using the reviewed items, with the existing filesystem checks and protection against duplicate runs. - Applications now has a prominent "All apps" entry on its start screen and results, with the total app count. Opening it clears an old search and the unused-app filter without losing your selection. - Before removing selected apps that are open, Nora lists them and asks permission to quit. Apps can ask you to save your work; an app that stays open or opens after confirmation is skipped. - The verified official Mole installer is pinned to 1.61.0. The compatibility audit and its limits are recorded in `docs/audits/2026-10-18-mole-1.61-compat.md`.
### Fixed - Uninstall uses the application's name rather than its Homebrew package token, reads Mole 1.61's personal-data selection and `[Brew]` groups, and authenticates Homebrew removals when required. Settings and personal data are included in the visible review; execution still requires the exact reviewed app and file list. Unknown, truncated or changed output is rejected before removal. - History no longer counts dry-run estimates as space freed or completed actions. Performance recognizes Mole 1.61's disk-verification skip message.
### Змінено - Натискання «Очистити кошик» одразу запускає очищення й закриває нагадування. Прибрано повторне сканування, окреме підтвердження, затримку кнопки та очікування результату. Очищення триває у фоні за вже показаним списком, зі збереженням перевірок файлової системи й захисту від повторного запуску. - На початковому екрані «Програми» та в результатах з'явився помітний перехід «Всі програми» із загальною кількістю. Перехід очищає попередній пошук і фільтр невикористовуваних програм, зберігаючи ваш вибір. - Перед видаленням відкритих програм Nora показує їхній список і просить дозволити завершення. Програми можуть запропонувати зберегти роботу; програма, яка залишилася відкритою або відкрилася після підтвердження, пропускається. - Перевірений офіційний інсталятор Mole оновлено до 1.61.0. Результати та межі перевірки сумісності описано в `docs/audits/2026-10-18-mole-1.61-compat.md`.
### Виправлено - Видалення використовує назву програми замість назви пакета Homebrew, розуміє новий вибір особистих даних і групи `[Brew]` у Mole 1.61, а за потреби отримує права адміністратора для видалення через Homebrew. Налаштування й особисті дані включені до видимого перегляду; виконання потребує точного збігу програми та списку файлів. Невідомий, обрізаний або змінений вивід зупиняє видалення. - Історія більше не зараховує оцінки попереднього перегляду до звільненого місця й виконаних дій. Обслуговування розпізнає нове повідомлення Mole 1.61 про пропущену перевірку диска.

A safety audit of every module, and a reminder for the Trash. The audit's main change is that Nora now refuses to act, instead of guessing, when Mole's output or a file's state cannot be trusted: an incomplete or stale preview, an unreadable protection list or a failed save no longer leads to a removal or to a "done" screen.
### Added - Trash reminders. While Nora is running it notices new files in your home Trash (`~/.Trash`; external disks are not looked at) and offers a review in a small panel. Settings has a switch for the reminders, and "Review home Trash…" in Nora's menu works with them off. The reminder never deletes anything: after the review, "Delete permanently" is a separate step with its own confirmation that says it cannot be undone, and its button stays inert for the first moments after it appears, so the second click of a double-click on "Empty Trash…" cannot reach it. Only the items you reviewed are removed; files that reach the Trash later are left alone, and if the Trash changed since the review you review it again. Stopping part-way leaves what was already deleted deleted. If an interruption leaves items set aside, deletion stays blocked until Nora has restored them. The result counts the entries removed, not freed space: the size shown is a logical size and can differ from the disk space returned. After a successful deletion the panel closes by itself after a few seconds; any other result (stopped, changed, failed, needs recovery) stays until you dismiss it. - The repository now runs the MoleKit and app tests on GitHub for every push to `main`.
### Changed - Decorative glass animation is bounded: at most 24 frames a second, a smaller swing (up to 18°) and fewer layers on the busy hero, with a lighter shadow and a tinted edge. It stops completely while the window is inactive or hidden and when Reduce Motion is on. - The console opens on the last command of the current module, with a History picker, pause and "jump to latest"; scrolling by hand stops following the output, and a shortened log says so. - The README states the limits of the checks: Cleanup and Projects use Mole commands that rescan rather than run a fixed list of paths, so a file that appears after the check can still be affected. See `docs/audits/2026-10-17-remediation.uk.md`.
### Fixed - Cleanup, Projects and Installers previews are rejected, not shown, when the list is incomplete, older than the last scan, has duplicate or ambiguous rows, or is empty without Mole saying so. An Installers scan that exits with an error no longer reads as "no installers". A file name with two spaces in a row is no longer cut short, and the final confirmation is sent only after the whole prompt has arrived and matches your selection exactly. - Cleanup no longer reports the size of a preview as space freed; without a report from Mole the result says it is unverified. Projects, Installers and Performance no longer promise space they did not measure. - Review shows every warning Mole gave, and the Full Disk Access explanation stays available. - If restoring the protection list fails, Nora shows it with a Retry button and blocks the next run. When something else changed the protection file meanwhile, both versions are kept and you are asked to reconcile them. If the defaults cannot be read, Protection cannot be edited over them, and a failed save is rolled back. - Smart Care and Cleanup no longer show a stale scan or results after Start over or a new scan, and Done returns to Smart Care when you came from there. Clean, Run and Remove stay visible but disabled with the reason, the found size is kept apart from the selected size, and error tiles have Retry. Opening the console no longer hides the action button. - Space Map no longer counts a folder and its contents twice, and refuses a stale or failed load. Tools checks Touch ID setup by its exit status and shows errors. Uninstall confirms the app and its helpers are gone, a malformed Homebrew reply is rejected, and updates that were blocked or stopped are not counted as done. - Security: a failed `launchctl` status check stops the action, and a quarantine that unloaded an agent but could not move it says so. Notices from manual database updates now show in Settings. - History shows a loading state and, when Mole fails, an error with Retry instead of an empty dashboard. Checking the latest Mole release shows the failure with Retry. Commands from Tools, Security, History and Space Map are logged under their own module, so "see console" no longer opens an empty log. - "Update Mole" is named for what it does, and a successful exit is no longer presented as proof that a new version is installed. - Space Map's Start over no longer takes Command-[ from Back, and Performance's Run is disabled when there is nothing to do. - Checkboxes in Space Map and Security, the external-drive picker and the selected sidebar item now have accessible names and traits.

Nora now uses far less CPU when none of it is on screen. In 1.2.0 a closed or hidden window could keep it at up to a third of a CPU core in the background; the same situations now measure under 1%.
### Added - The quick menu's Processor tile shows the CPU temperature with the same coloured dot as the menu bar (green below 70 °C, orange from 70 °C, red from 90 °C), whether or not the menu bar shows it; the tooltip gives the value in degrees. It is read every 3 seconds, only while the menu is open.
### Fixed - After the quick menu had been opened once, Nora kept drawing it in the background on every status sample and kept Mole's status stream running, even with every window closed: about 14% of a CPU core plus 1% for the stream, all the time. The menu now exists only while it is open, and the stream stops 10 seconds after it closes. The list of apps by memory is read every 3 seconds while the menu is open, not on every redraw. - System Status kept Mole's status stream and its live readings (`nettop`, `lsof`, the chip's sensors) running while its window was minimised, covered or on another Space, and redrew every card on every sample: with the window on another Space that took about 13% of Nora's main thread. They now run only while the window is on screen and resume when it comes back. - Spinners (in cards, next to a busy module in the sidebar and on the round button) redrew the whole window at the display's refresh rate, and went on when the window was minimised or on another Space. A spinner left turning in a hidden window could keep Nora at up to 38% of a core. Spinners now turn at up to 30 frames a second and stop while their window is not on screen; the same case measures under 1%. - With CPU or memory figures in the menu bar, Mole's status stream runs all the time, and System Status, Space Map or History left as the last screen in the closed window redrew on every sample: 23% of a core with nothing on screen. Samples now reach a screen only while it is on screen; the menu bar title reads them directly. The same state measures 0.7%. - With the main window closed, the round button's mouse monitors went on waking Nora for mouse moves in every other app. They now stop when the window closes and come back when it is on screen again. - The quick menu showed a cache of zero as "Zero KB" (in Ukrainian "Нуль КБ"); every size of zero now reads as a number, "0 KB".
